name: reference_contract
description: One authored field that names rows in another type, declared so the naming can be checked. Friendly authoring stays friendly -- an author types or picks names -- and the runtime stops splitting comma-separated strings and hoping they still name something. A reference that no longer resolves is the failure this exists to make impossible to land quietly: a world naming a source that was removed renders less and says nothing, which is indistinguishable from a source that answered with nothing. A reference may name a row in another type, or a column of one: surface_pattern.item_fields names columns of whichever table that same row's reads_type points at, so the target type is read from a field rather than declared as a literal. A pattern backed by an organ rather than a table names no columns at all and is skipped rather than reported broken.
